text:
morgan: Quick design check — on the Create Deployment modal we've shipped, I'm seeing a few UX/AX problems around error signaling and destructive actions. Can we do a rapid pass? :eyes:

priya: yep, saw that. which screen specifically?

morgan: the modal with name, replica count, and optional config file upload. When validation fails it shows inline red text under the field, but then also a small toast. Users miss the inline when the modal is tall.

dan: can you paste a screenshot?

morgan: https://img.redwood.mock/screens/deploy-modal-errors.png

marie: first thought — inline is good for field-level issues but we need a persistent summary at the top for visibility when the modal scrolls. The summary should link to fields.

tay: +1 for a summary. Also the required marker is an asterisk with no accessible label. VoiceOver reads nothing helpful. :warning:

accessibility-bot: a11y note: required indicators must have text or use `aria-labelledby` on the field. Otherwise screen readers can't infer requiredness.

priya: what about using inline + top summary, and when the modal is scrolled collapse the inline into the summary?

morgan: I like that. Another issue — destructive action: there's a "Delete template" button next to a small text link. It's easy to misclick when you're editing. We should consider a stronger guard and typed confirmation for bulk removes.

dan: for single deletes a confirm modal with clear copy is fine. For bulk, typed confirm (e.g., type DELETE) + a red full-width CTA is safer.

marie: can we avoid interrupting flow for low-risk deletes? Maybe use a softer inline confirmation for one-off deletes and typed confirm only for >5 items or if data is irreversible.

tay: accessibility nit — when the summary appears, we should announce it via `aria-live="assertive"` so screen reader users are told there are errors. Right now nothing announces.

priya: good call. Also the color contrast of the inline helper is only 3.8:1 on dark mode — need >=4.5:1 for small text.

morgan: ugh — okay so next steps I propose:
- add a persistent error summary at the top of the modal that links to fields
- keep inline errors but hide them from view when scrolled; summary remains visible and focuses the first error when clicked
- implement `aria-live` announcement on summary
- revisit required marker (add visually-hidden "required" text + tooltip)
- tighten delete guard: soft confirm for single deletes, typed confirm for bulk irreversible ops

aisha: copy suggestion for the summary: "We found problems with your deployment details. Please fix the fields below to continue." Short and consistent with other modals.

morgan: nice. For typed confirm copy: "Type DELETE to permanently remove these templates."

dan: technical note for implementation: when linking summary -> field, use `element.scrollIntoView({behavior: 'smooth', block: 'center'})` then focus the input. Avoid focus trap breaking by ensuring modal remains the active element.

accessibility-bot: also ensure focus is set to the summary on submit error so keyboard users land at the error entrypoint.

priya: design question — do we visually show the asterisk for required fields or move to explicit "Required" label for each field? Asterisk is compact but ambiguous for some users.

marie: if space allows, explicit "(required)" text is clearer and better for discovery. We can make it visually lighter but still present in the DOM.

tay: we should also add a unit test for screen reader flow in the QA ticket — e.g., assert that `aria-live` region gets the message on submit and that focus moves to summary.

morgan: sounds good. I'll mock a quick variant with summary + inline and update the Figma. I'll also add copy and a11y tasks to the ticket.

dan: tagging infra: @ui-bot deploy-preview would help — want to test keyboard/voiceover on the actual component.

ui-bot: deploy-preview scheduled for staging at 2026-04-02 14:00 UTC.

morgan: perfect. Thanks all — I'll post the Figma link when ready. :thumbsup:

priya: thanks — leaving a note to keep confirmation thresholds configurable for product teams.

marie: small polish: add a short animation when summary appears (fade + translateY) so it catches the eye but doesn't shift layout harshly.

morgan: noted. Will prototype without layout jump. End of thread.
